quote: return [];  // storage blocked or corrupt: start empty; app.js tells the user
title: Unreadable or old-shape saved data loads as an empty list, nothing tells the user, and the next save erases it
evidence: store.js:9 returns [] on any parse error. store.js:7 silently drops every record without a string `name`. The comment says app.js tells the user, but app.js:3 only does `let recipes = loadRecipes();` and no code shows a message at load. app.js:23-24 then pushes onto that empty list and saveRecipes overwrites the key.
failing_case: localStorage 'recipes' holds a truncated write (`[{"id":"1","name":"Soup"`) or a previous shape (`[{"title":"Soup","minutes":30}]`). The page opens showing 'No recipes yet'. The user adds one recipe, setItem replaces the old value, and the earlier recipes are gone with no warning and no copy kept.
remediation: Return a status from loadRecipes (ok, corrupt, blocked, dropped count). Show it in the status region on load. Keep the raw string under a backup key before the first overwrite. Version the saved shape and migrate old records.

title: Deleting an item destroys the focused button and focus falls to the page top
evidence: render() (app.js:10) replaces the whole list through innerHTML. The focused Delete button is removed from the DOM, so document.activeElement becomes body. Nothing moves focus afterwards.
failing_case: A keyboard user tabs to the Delete button on the fifth recipe and confirms. Focus resets to the start of the document. They must tab through the heading, the form and the list again to reach the next Delete (WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order).
remediation: After the delete, focus the next item's Delete button, or the previous one, or the list heading when the list is empty. Add tabindex=-1 to the heading if it is the target.

title: Delete ignores the save result and reports 'Deleted' when storage failed
evidence: saveRecipes returns false on error (store.js:17-19). The add handler checks it (app.js:24-25), but the delete handler at app.js:35 discards it and app.js:36 always announces 'Deleted'.
failing_case: Storage is full or blocked (private mode, quota). The user deletes 'Soup'. The status says Deleted “Soup”. and the item disappears, but localStorage is unchanged, so Soup returns on the next load.
remediation: Branch on the return value, as the add handler does. On failure, say the delete was not saved. Consider keeping the item until the write succeeds.

quote: return Array.isArray(data) ? data.filter((r) => r && typeof r.name === "string") : [];
title: Loader accepts records with no id or no numeric minutes, so delete crashes and the total becomes NaN or a string
evidence: The only check is `typeof r.name === "string"`. A record without `id` renders as data-id="undefined" (app.js:10, escapeHtml(undefined) gives 'undefined'). app.js:32 `recipes.find((x) => x.id === id)` then compares undefined to 'undefined' and returns undefined, and app.js:33 calls describe(undefined), which throws at app.js:15. The comment at app.js:14 ('never null') is false for loaded data. totalMinutes (store.js:23) adds r.minutes unchecked.
failing_case: Saved data `[{"name":"Soup"}]` (or a numeric id, or minutes saved as "30"). Click Delete on Soup: TypeError 'Cannot read properties of undefined', no confirm, and the record cannot be removed. Add a recipe: the status says 'Total cooking time: NaN minutes' (missing minutes), or '030...' concatenated (string minutes).
remediation: Add one normaliser in loadRecipes that coerces id to a string (generate one if missing), requires a finite positive minutes, and drops or repairs the rest. Guard `r` in the delete handler.

title: parseInt reads '1e2' as 1 although the number input accepts it as 100
evidence: input type=number (index.html:17) accepts exponent notation and passes validation. input.value stays '1e2'. parseInt('1e2', 10) returns 1.
failing_case: The user types 1e2 into Minutes and saves. The recipe is stored as 1 minute and the status shows a total that is off by 99.
remediation: Use `valueAsNumber` or Number(value) and require Number.isInteger and the 1..600 range in the handler.

quote: button { font: inherit; padding: 10px 16px; margin-top: 12px; background: var(--accent); color: #fff; border: 0; min-height: 44px; }
title: Delete buttons inherit the form button's margin-top, so each row sits 12px low
evidence: .del (styles.css:10) overrides only margin-left, so margin-top:12px and min-height:44px from line 7 apply inside each <li>. The text sits at the top of the line and the 44px button is pushed below the baseline, which makes the rows taller than the text. Traced from the CSS; not driven because Bash was unavailable.
failing_case: Open the list with any recipe: the name and minutes sit higher than the Delete button, and the row is about 56px tall.
remediation: Scope the margin to the form button (`form button`) or set `.del { margin-top: 0; vertical-align: middle; }`, or lay the row out with flex and align-items:center.
